culture.title: Mark Matariki as the Cluster Rises
culture.description: The Māori new year, marked across the city with dawn ceremonies, hautapu offerings and light installations when the Matariki cluster returns in midwinter.
culture.bonus: Find the cluster yourself before dawn — low in the northeast.

culture.title: A New Zealand Play at the Waterfront Theatre
culture.description: Auckland Theatre Company's purpose-built house in Wynyard Quarter, programming new New Zealand writing alongside the big international titles.
culture.bonus: Book the front of the circle rather than the stalls.

culture.title: New Material Night at The Classic
culture.description: The hundred-seat Queen Street room where every New Zealand comedian you have heard of worked out their first ten minutes, still running new material nights midweek.
culture.bonus: Sit anywhere except the front row.

culture.title: Climb Into a Flying Boat at MOTAT
culture.description: Two Western Springs sites full of working machinery — Pearse's 1903 aeroplane, a Solent flying boat you can walk through, and volunteers who restored most of it themselves.
culture.bonus: Ride the heritage tram between the two sites.

culture.title: Eat Your Way Through Pasifika Festival
culture.description: The largest Pacific festival on earth takes over Western Springs each March — island villages with their own stages, kitchens and kava, spread across the whole park.
culture.bonus: Eat in every village. It can be done in one day.

culture.title: Walk the Tunnels Under North Head
culture.description: A volcanic headland at Devonport honeycombed with Victorian and Second World War gun emplacements, with unlit tunnels you can walk straight into and the whole harbour on top.
culture.bonus: Bring a torch — the tunnels are unlit and go a long way in.

culture.title: Hear the APO at the Aotea Centre
culture.description: The Auckland Philharmonia in the Aotea Centre — a full professional orchestra with student and under-30 tickets that cost less than a round of drinks.
culture.bonus: Try a short rush-hour concert if a full programme feels like too much.

culture.title: Meet Hotunui at the Auckland Museum
culture.description: Tāmaki Paenga Hira holds Hotunui, a carved meeting house from 1878, and Te Toki a Tāpiri, the last great Māori war canoe — both under one neoclassical roof in the Domain.
culture.bonus: Stay for the Māori cultural performance inside Hotunui.

chill.title: Soak in the Geothermal Pools at Parakai
chill.description: Geothermal pools an hour northwest of the city where the water comes out of the ground at sixty degrees — deeply unglamorous and exactly right on a wet Sunday.
chill.bonus: Do the hydroslide at least once, unironically.

chill.title: Gallery Afternoon in Titirangi Village
chill.description: Te Uru is a contemporary gallery perched above the Manukau in Titirangi, all glass and native bush, with arguably the best gallery view in the country.
chill.bonus: Drive down to Cornwallis wharf afterwards.

chill.title: Sunset on the Manukau at Ambury Farm
chill.description: A working farm on the Manukau foreshore twenty minutes from the CBD — sheep on the path, godwits on the mudflats, and a sunset over the Waitākeres with nobody else there.
chill.bonus: Time it for low tide and walk out onto the shell banks.

chill.title: A Slow Day on Onetangi Beach
chill.description: Waiheke's longest beach, forty minutes by ferry and a bus from the wharf — two kilometres of white sand, warm water and a bar at either end.
chill.bonus: Walk the entire length of the sand before you have a drink.

chill.title: Swim the Saltwater Pool at Parnell Baths
chill.description: A 1950s saltwater pool cut into the rock above Judges Bay, filled straight from the harbour and painted with a mural you can see from the motorway.
chill.bonus: Swim one length underwater along the mural wall.

chill.title: Friday Night Film at Silo Park
chill.description: Summer Fridays in the shadow of a disused cement silo in Wynyard Quarter — food trucks, a record fair, and a film projected onto the silo wall once it is properly dark.
chill.bonus: Get there early enough to claim the beanbags.

8ball.title: Board Whichever Ferry Leaves Next
8ball.description: Go to the Downtown Ferry Terminal, take whichever sailing departs next — Devonport, Bayswater, Half Moon Bay, Rakino — and give that place the rest of your afternoon.
8ball.bonus: Don't look up what's there before you land.

8ball.title: Pick a Volcano You've Never Climbed
8ball.description: Fifty-three volcanoes sit underneath this city. Pick a cone you have never been up — Māngere, Ōwairaka, Te Tātua-a-Riukiuta — and be on the summit for sunset.
8ball.bonus: Name every other cone you can see from the top.

social.title: Eat Standing Up at the Night Markets
social.description: A different mall carpark fills with a hundred food stalls every night of the week — Malaysian, Korean, Uyghur, dessert trucks, and half of Auckland eating on its feet.
social.bonus: Order one thing you cannot identify.

social.title: Carafes on the Kerb at Freida Margolis
social.description: A former West Lynn butcher's shop turned tiny wine bar — Colombian playlists, cheap carafes, and the whole crowd spilling onto the footpath by six.
social.bonus: Sit outside on the kerb like everyone else does.

social.title: Warriors Game at Go Media Stadium
social.description: NRL at Mount Smart, where the Warriors crowd is the best-natured sporting mob in the country and the terrace sings for eighty minutes regardless of the scoreline.
social.bonus: Join the Up The Wahs chant. You will know when.

social.title: Rooftop Beers and Bowling at Dr Rudi's
social.description: A rooftop brewpub on the Viaduct with its own tanks behind the bar, a bowling alley upstairs and a deck that holds the last of the afternoon sun.

social.title: Super Rugby Under the Lights at Eden Park
social.description: The Blues at Eden Park — fifty thousand people, a whole suburb emptying into the ground on foot, and the loudest stadium in New Zealand.
social.bonus: Learn one chant before kickoff so you can join in.

social.title: Catch a Gig at The Powerstation
social.description: An old Mount Eden power substation turned 900-capacity live room — low ceiling, sticky floor, and the venue every touring band plays before they outgrow it.
social.bonus: Get on the mezzanine rail for the encore.

social.title: Order Off No Menu at Caretaker
social.description: A dark basement bar under Britomart with no drinks list at all — you describe a mood or a spirit and the bartender builds something in front of you.
social.bonus: Give them one word and nothing else to work with.

social.title: Work Your Way Around Ponsonby Central
social.description: A converted warehouse block off Ponsonby Road holding a dozen kitchens and bars that open onto shared laneways — the default Friday for half the inner west.
social.bonus: Eat from two kitchens and drink at a third.

foodie.title: Dumpling Crawl Down Dominion Road
foodie.description: Balmoral's stretch of Dominion Road is Auckland's Chinatown — start at Barilla Dumpling and work your way down the street until you physically cannot continue.
foodie.bonus: Three shops minimum, and order the pan-fried at each one.

foodie.title: The Tasting Menu at Paris Butter
foodie.description: A small Herne Bay villa doing the most precise cooking in the country — French technique, New Zealand produce, and a menu worth planning a whole evening around.
foodie.bonus: Take the wine pairing and let the sommelier choose blind.

foodie.title: Shuck-to-Order Oysters at Depot Eatery
foodie.description: Al Brown's no-bookings Federal Street institution — oysters opened in front of you, wood-fired small plates, and a room that has been full every night for over a decade.
foodie.bonus: Order the turbot sliders and a dozen Clevedon oysters.

foodie.title: Eat Wild Game at Cazador
foodie.description: A family-run game restaurant on Dominion Road serving wild venison, goat, hare and pigeon, with a charcuterie counter that quietly supplies half the city.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever is on the board that you have never eaten before.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Amano Before the Queue
foodie.description: A cavernous brick bakery-restaurant in Britomart milling its own flour for the sourdough and rolling pasta by hand in the window.
foodie.bonus: Buy a loaf from the bakery counter on the way out.

foodie.title: Long Lunch in the Hallertau Beer Garden
foodie.description: A brewery garden out at Riverhead, thirty minutes from town — long tables under the trees, a wood-fired kitchen and eight taps of beer brewed on site.
foodie.bonus: Take the tasting paddle out onto the lawn.

foodie.title: Fire-Cooked New Zealand Produce at Ahi
foodie.description: Ben Bayly cooks a genuinely New Zealand menu over open fire — Te Matuku oysters, kelp, horopito, Hawke's Bay lamb — with the harbour through the glass at Commercial Bay.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the pass and watch the grill instead of the view.

foodie.title: Saturday Morning at Ōtara Flea Market
foodie.description: The largest Pacific market in the country fills a South Auckland carpark every Saturday — Tongan ʻota ʻika, Samoan panipopo, umu cooking and a brass band by nine.
foodie.bonus: Get a coconut bun and a raw fish from two different stalls.

adventure.title: Walk the Coast to Coast Across the Isthmus
adventure.description: Sixteen kilometres from the Waitematā to the Manukau, straight over four volcanic cones and through the Domain — the whole isthmus on foot in a morning.
adventure.bonus: Finish with a swim at Onehunga Bay.

adventure.title: Ocean-Touch Bungy Off the Harbour Bridge
adventure.description: Forty metres off the Auckland Harbour Bridge on the only ocean-touch bungy in the world — ask for the dip and they drop you into the Waitematā to your shoulders.
adventure.bonus: Take the water touch. Don't think about it at the top.

adventure.title: Day Trip to Tiritiri Matangi Bird Sanctuary
adventure.description: A predator-free island sanctuary 75 minutes by ferry where takahē, kōkako and saddleback walk the tracks beside you and the dawn chorus is genuinely deafening.
adventure.bonus: Spot a takahē — there are only a few hundred left alive.

adventure.title: Stand in the Middle of the Muriwai Gannet Colony
adventure.description: A thousand pairs of gannets nest on the cliff stacks at Muriwai and the boardwalk puts you metres away while they dive-bomb the surf below.
adventure.bonus: Count how many manage to land without crashing.

adventure.title: Cross the Dunes to Lake Wainamu
adventure.description: Walk up a stream bed and over black sand dunes to a freshwater lake hidden behind the wildest beach in the Waitākeres, then swim in both in one afternoon.
adventure.bonus: Sandboard the big dune on the way back out.

adventure.title: A Weekend Under the Great Barrier Dark Sky
adventure.description: Aotea / Great Barrier is one of a handful of International Dark Sky Sanctuaries on earth — no streetlights, no power grid, and a Milky Way bright enough to cast shadows.
adventure.bonus: Find the Magellanic Clouds with your naked eye.

adventure.title: Snorkel the Kelp at Goat Island Marine Reserve
adventure.description: New Zealand's first marine reserve, 90 minutes north — wade straight off the beach into kelp forest thick with snapper and blue maomao that have never been fished.
adventure.bonus: Feed them nothing, but stay still and let the snapper come to you.

adventure.title: Abseil the Waterfalls of Piha Canyon
adventure.description: Abseil down waterfalls, slide natural rock chutes and jump into bush pools in the rainforest canyons behind Piha, an hour from the CBD.
adventure.bonus: Jump the last drop instead of abseiling it.
